problem: The sentence 'set gain so small hand motions make large object motions only when needed' is ambiguous. It mixes up two opposite needs: coarse travel (where you want amplification) and fine placement (where you want a small, 1:1 or reduced mapping). A student can read it either way.
fix: Set the gain from the job: use gain above 1 (small hand motion, large object motion) for coarse travel across a big scene, and gain near 1 or below it for fine placement, so precision is not lost.

problem: The answer lists 'a lower gain' as a way to reduce fatigue. A lower gain means more hand travel for the same object movement, so it increases arm movement and fatigue. This also contradicts the design rule in Section 3 that asks for amplification when large object motion is needed.
fix: Replace 'a lower gain' with 'a higher gain for coarse moves, so less arm travel is needed, with gain near 1 only for fine placement'. Keep the prop, arm rest and confirm-on-release points.

problem: q is described as 'the closest point on the ray', but q = p + t u with t = (c − p)·u is the closest point on the infinite line. When t < 0 the closest point on the actual ray is p, not q. The selection test t ≥ 0 hides this, but the definition as written is loose.
fix: Write: q = p + t u is the closest point on the ray's line; the ray selects the sphere when t ≥ 0 (centre in front of the origin) and d = ||c − q|| ≤ R. If t < 0 the centre lies behind the ray origin and the object is not selected.
